claims.claim: Russ concludes that Operation Ares is a failure, shadowy and inconclusive.
claims.source: Joanna Russ, F&SF, vol. 40 no. 4, April 1971, p. 69, reprinted in CLC
claims.quote: the novel is a failure, shadowy and inconclusive

claims.claim: Somtow Sucharitkul argues it is the familiarity of Wolfe's sources rather than the baroque weirdness of his textures that makes The Sword of the Lictor powerful.
claims.source: Somtow Sucharitkul, "A Certain Slant of 'I'", Fantasy Newsletter, vol. 4 no. 12, December 1981, pp. 16-17, reprinted in CLC
claims.quote: not the baroque weirdness of its textures

claims.claim: Sucharitkul says Wolfe's neologisms mingle with resurrected antique words and hybridizations of Latin, Greek and Germanic roots.
claims.source: Somtow Sucharitkul, Fantasy Newsletter, vol. 4 no. 12, December 1981, p. 16, reprinted in CLC
claims.quote: neologisms mingle with resurrected antique words

claims.claim: Clute allows that for some readers the first three volumes may have seemed picaresque and somewhat random in nature.
claims.source: John Clute, 'The Urth and All Its Glory', reprinted in CLC
claims.quote: may have seemed picaresque, somewhat random in nature

claims.claim: The thread's opening poster says The Book of the New Sun was a very hard read whose plots did not link well.
claims.source: 'Belgarion', SFFWorld forum thread 'Gene Wolfe Sucks!', 25 September 2002
claims.quote: It was a very hard read, the plots did not link

claims.claim: The opening poster says the quartet was basically a collection of short stories.
claims.quote: was basically a collection of short stories

claims.claim: A forum reader reports the series held his interest but left him feeling that he missed a lot.
claims.quote: I had the feeling that I missed a lot

claims.claim: A forum defender argues the style is one of the key selling points of The Book of the New Sun while conceding it could turn some readers off.
claims.quote: the style is one of the key selling-points

claims.claim: Allbery says he would not recommend The Urth of the New Sun even to someone who read the original series.
claims.source: Russ Allbery, review of The Urth of the New Sun, 10 September 2004
claims.quote: I don't think I would recommend this book even to someone

claims.claim: Allbery concludes he is not sure the series quite lived up to the promise of its beginning.
claims.source: Russ Allbery, review of The Citadel of the Autarch, 28 June 2004
claims.quote: I'm not sure that this series quite lived up to the promise

claims.claim: Brian Murphy writes that half the reviews of The Book of the New Sun are by people who do not seem to understand what is going on yet declare that you have to read it.
claims.source: Brian Murphy, 'Gene Wolfe is intimidating. The Knight is not.', The Silver Key, 29 March 2025
claims.quote: people who don’t seem to understand what’s going on yet declare

claims.claim: The reviewer attributes the book's narrow readership to its reputation of being dense, labyrinthine and outright incomprehensible at times.
claims.source: Tachy, 'Review: The Book of the New Sun'
claims.quote: being dense, labyrinthine, and outright incomprehensible at times

claims.claim: The reviewer reports that characters in the book are often described as one-dimensional and bewildering.
claims.source: Tachy, 'Review: The Book of the New Sun'

claims.claim: Roy C. Lackey rejects the cross-book explanation of the missing guard, saying the theory cannot be true.
claims.source: Roy C. Lackey, Urth mailing list, '(urth) Close Reading: Torturer' thread, 2006-09-05 (message 002927)
claims.quote: so neat it *ought* to be true. But it can't be.

claims.claim: The reader 'nastler' identifies a recurring tableau of a beast man, an armed man and a woman first appearing in chapter one.
claims.source: 'nastler', Urth mailing list, '(urth) Close Reading: Torturer' thread, 2006-09-06 (message 002936)
claims.quote: Also in this chapter the first (but not last)
